subject: Post-call: technical qualification — chat vs completions, tokenization & streaming
messages:
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>
To: Alex Tran <alex.tran@polestar.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-07-18T14:05:00-07:00
Subject: Post-call: technical qualification — chat vs completions, tokenization & streaming

Hi Alex — thanks again for the demo time today. Quick recap and our proposed next steps so we can align engineering teams: 

Summary of needs we heard
- Low-latency conversational endpoint for user-facing chat (multiturn, tool calling in phase 2)
- Batch reranker for convert-score on candidate responses (embeddings + lightweight rerank model)
- Tight control over token budget and deterministic stop semantics for system messages
- Enterprise auth (OIDC + service-account fallback) and region pinning to us-west for compliance

Open technical questions (we raised these in the call; please confirm):
1) Chat vs completions: do you need streaming token-by-token in the client for perceived responsiveness, or would you prefer server-side streaming to Redwood's SDK with chunked delivery to clients?
2) Tokenization: are you standardizing on UTF-8 byte-pair tokenization for your legacy models, or will you adopt a unigram/subword tokenizer we should account for in our prompt/token accounting?
3) Max_tokens & stops: what's the strictest max_tokens cap per user message you want enforced at the gateway (client) vs. at the runtime? Any hard stop tokens we should add to avoid leaking PII?
4) Reranker workflow: do you plan to compute candidate embeddings on the client and send them, or want Redwood to host a candidate-embedding service with short-lived cache keys?

Proposed next steps
- Karthik and Marissa to produce a short integration plan (SDK onboarding, auth flows, routing policy) — target for EOD tomorrow
- We attach a lightweight request/response schema diagram (postcall_schema_v1.png) and a draft reranker spec (mvp_reranker_spec.pdf) for your engineers to review
- Tech sync (30m): Wed 10am PT — confirm if that works for you and Jamie

Attachments: postcall_schema_v1.png (diagram), mvp_reranker_spec.pdf (PDF)

Best,
Hannah

Subject: Re: Post-call: technical qualification — chat vs completions, tokenization & streaming

Thanks Hannah — useful summary. A couple quick clarifications from our side before the sync: 

- Streaming: client-side streaming is preferred for the chat UI, but we can accept server->client chunked streaming if latency is within 160ms median. We rely on partial tokens for progressive rendering.
- Tokenizer: we currently use a legacy BPE tokenizer (in-house variant). We're evaluating switching to a public BPE model but haven't committed. Important point: token counts in our audit correlate to user billing, so we need tight one-to-one accounting with Redwood's reported tokens.
- Max tokens: can you enforce both a soft and a hard cap? Soft cap for optimization (early truncation warnings) and hard cap to drop extra tokens before hits billing. Also we have a stop sequence: "--END--" that should always be honored when present.
- Reranker: we prefer Redwood to host candidate embeddings and offer a short-lived cache keyed to request IDs (so we don't upload entire candidate sets every request). That would reduce client's bandwidth.

Jamie (cc) will bring our infra lead on the Wed sync. Wed 10am PT works.

Alex

Subject: Re: Post-call: technical qualification — chat vs completions, tokenization & streaming

Alex — perfect, thanks for the specifics. Quick answers inline and some implementation suggestions for Wed's sync: 

1) Streaming semantics
- Redwood supports server-side streaming (LLM->runtime->SDK chunks) and client-initiated streaming (SDK proxies tokens as they arrive). For 160ms median target, we recommend server-side with our continuous-batching disabled for that route and a per-route low-latency mode. We'll provide a sample SDK flag: streaming: "client_forwarding": true/false.

2) Tokenization / accounting
- We can surface token counts in two ways: at request-level (total_tokens) and per-message token_breakdown. For billing alignment, we'll enable a tokenization hook that runs your tokenizer code in a sandbox during the preflight step so counts match exactly. That requires a small wasm module or an agreed tokenizer spec (we can host the canonical tokenizer).

3) Max_tokens / stop semantics
- We support soft/hard caps via routing policy: soft_cap (warn at N% of budget in response metadata) and hard_cap (truncation before generation). We can also register explicit stop sequences (e.g., "--END--") and ensure deterministic truncation. For PII redaction, we can add an optional post-generation filter pipeline configured per-route.

4) Reranker: embedding hosting
- Redwood can host candidate embeddings and expose a short-lived cache API keyed by request_id. Flow: client sends document IDs, Redwood generates embeddings (or ingests precomputed), stores for TTL (e.g., 5m), and the reranker pulls them for scoring. We'll share a sample API contract in the integration plan.

Attachments referenced: postcall_schema_v1.png (shows proposed HTTP request/response fields for both chat and completions), mvp_reranker_spec.pdf (reranker flow + cache TTLs).

I'll loop in the SDK snippet and a suggested route config in a follow-up note before the Wed meeting. Anything else urgent to add to the agenda?

Thanks — Hannah

Looping in a brief note from an engineering ops perspective (will expand in the integration plan):
- SDK/auth: recommend using our OIDC-first flow with a service-account JWT fallback for server-to-server. We'll include code samples for short-lived tokens and automatic refresh.
- Routing: for the chat route, tag requests with "latency_slo=160ms" and set router policy to prefer local us-west pools; fallback to a quantized model variant if capacity triggers.
- Schema: use a lightweight JSON envelope for the chat path with fields: request_id, user_id (hashed), messages[], streaming (bool), max_tokens, stop_sequences[]. See postcall_schema_v1.png for field names.

I'll have the detailed integration doc and sample SDK snippet uploaded to the Drive link by EOD tomorrow. Looking forward to the sync.
